findings.where: Screen 6 text and read, and whatAmILookingAt Screen 6
findings.what: "Only the reactances of the set and the board limit the surge that gap drives" is an absolute; the fact-check already narrowed the same claim in explain.text to "the main limit", but the screen still says "Only", so change it to match.

findings.where: practice.text (the by-hand list) and contested: null
findings.what: The brief says where to close is taught as contested: about 11 o'clock in one source and about 5 minutes to 12 in another, both slowly in the FAST direction. The lesson drops this (contested is null), and the by-hand list tells Dan to send the close "that far before 12", a 1.8 degree lead, which is 50 ms at 0.1 Hz and too short to time by hand; teach the manual close point as the sources give it and keep the computed advance angle for the relay and the synchroniser.

"Then the set picks up a little load as it closes" stops short of the reason: closed while running slow, the set would be driven as a motor, which reverse power protection sees (lesson 7); add that one sentence.

findings.where: practice.text, "Send the close once, that far before 12, and let go"
findings.what: "Let go" has no reason; one sentence on what goes wrong if the close is held while the pointer turns would make it stick.

The windows appear as one set of example settings, but the lesson never says that makers set them differently, from about 0.5% to 5% on voltage and 0.1 to 0.5 Hz on slip; one sentence would carry the brief's "a maker's setting, never a constant".

The demonstration shows only the late close (pressed at 12, shut at 3.6 degrees FAST), while the cure, pressing 3.6 degrees early so the breaker shuts at 12, is only told; nothing shows it until the relay on screen 12, so a second press at the advance angle would show the cause and its cure side by side.

"Swap two of the set's phases, B and C" and "Turn the relay on" ask Dan to do something already done, because each screen opens with that switch on; word them as what is now set, for example "B and C are now swapped".

Dan answers "No, the phase sequence is wrong" and the screen then shuts the breaker anyway with only "That's it."; give the step a right line such as "Here is what closing would do." so the red bars read as the consequence, not a reaction to his answer.

Both bars turn red for a 9 degree close whose surge is only about 0.6 per unit, because the slip is outside the window; the sentence below explains this, but a red, nearly empty bar can read as a big surge, so consider marking the window breach apart from the bar colour.
"Shut at 180 degrees and the surge reaches 8.0" drops the unit; say 8.0 per unit, as the 5.7 two sentences earlier does.
The brief's one line ashore, BS 7671 Section 551's interlock against running a set in parallel with the supply, is missing, and it would link this lesson to the regulations Dan already holds.
The opening is a bare recall question with no picture, and screen 2 holds its picture still, so the first thing Dan can move arrives on screen 4.
